SIDE VIEW – cut away · from the fish’s right · scale 1.4 : 1
end hooks on ③ a stop
TOP VIEW – CUT THROUGH THE GEARS
dashed: ⑤ the 8 T under the 24 T · ⑦ damper below · pink = stand post
SAME MOTOR AS THE WIND-UP CAR – PLUS 3 EXTRAS
From your picture: the key ① winds the
spring ②; a stop ③ holds its outer end.
The spring turns the main gear ④, which
spins the small gear ⑤ fast. In the car ⑤
turns the wheels; here it turns a crank ⑥.
• a click, so winding doesn’t drive the gears
• ⑦ a grease damper: the car spends its energy
rolling; a fish standing still would spin out
1 Push the stop pin IN – it drops
3 Set the fish on its anemone stand.
4 Pull the stop pin OUT → the tail
5 Push the pin back in to stop.
The key turns slowly backwards while
No damper → it races, empty in < ½ s
⑦ Ø8 rotor, 2 mm gaps of 30 Pa·s
Damper ×2 or ÷2, double friction or a
5 main gear 36 T + click 6 gear 8 + 24 T
7 crank pinion 8 T + crank + damper rotor
All printed + a dab of damping grease
Stop pin is captive: it pulls out but
Opening the head lets the spring go
Snap fits: no glue, no tools
Clownfish don’t cruise: they hover beside their anemone,
sculling with quick tail beats. This one does the same on its
anemone stand; its middle white band hides the tail joint.

Biomimicry – clownfish hovering at its anemone
